name: The Land of Kush
sourceName: The Land of Kush official website
ownershipEvidence: The official website explicitly states “Black-Owned & Baltimore Proud” and identifies Gregory and Naijha Wright-Brown in its origin story.
servicesSearchTerms: vegan food, soul food, plant-based meals, takeout, delivery, catering
notes: Official site confirms current physical address, phone, menu/service category, ownership designation, and HTTPS destination. Approximately nearby Baltimore city destination; distance was not used as an eligibility claim.

name: Paschal's
subcategory: soul food restaurant and event space
ownershipEvidence: Atlanta Eats identifies Paschal's as a place where one of America's greatest Black entrepreneurs built wealth, names founders James and Robert Paschal, and says James's son Curtis continues the family tradition at the current Castleberry Hill restaurant (https://www.atlantaeats.com/blog/black-owned-atl-paschals/). The New Georgia Encyclopedia independently documents the Paschal brothers' founding and calls the associated Paschal's Motor Hotel the first Black-owned hotel in Atlanta (https://www.georgiaencyclopedia.org/articles/arts-culture/paschals-restaurant/).
notes: Official site explicitly presents the current restaurant/event space and lists the numbered address and phone. Everyday food use; research-only candidate near Morehouse/AUC.

name: Paschal's
ownershipEvidence: Resy's Atlanta feature explicitly identifies Paschal's as a Black-owned restaurant and documents its Black entrepreneurship history (https://blog.resy.com/2020/05/black-owned-restaurants-atlanta/). Paschal's official site identifies founders James and Robert Paschal and the current restaurant address; the Georgia Encyclopedia (Emory University) independently documents the brothers' founding and Black-owned hotel history (https://www.georgiaencyclopedia.org/articles/arts-culture/paschals-restaurant/).
notes: Official homepage supplies current numbered address, phone, HTTPS destination, restaurant category, and hours. Near the Atlanta University Center/Spelman area; research only.

name: Lucille's
ownershipEvidence: Southern Foodways Alliance's Gravy identifies Chris Williams as the chef-owner of Lucille's and describes his Black Texan history; it states he opened the Houston restaurant with his brother Ben in 2012. https://www.southernfoodways.org/the-fine-legacy-of-lucilles/
notes: Official site provides the numbered address and describes the restaurant and its co-founders. Research only; no publication or live-listing claim.

name: The Breakfast Klub
ownershipEvidence: The official site identifies Marcus Davis as the entrepreneurial mastermind and Chief Steward of the parent company of The Breakfast Klub. The Houston Chronicle identifies Marcus Davis as owner and The Breakfast Klub as Black-owned: https://www.houstonchronicle.com/entertainment/dining/article/The-Breakfast-Klub-among-top-Black-owned-16828919.php
notes: Official site provides the numbered address, phone, current food-service description, and links to official social accounts. Research only; no publication or live-listing claim.

name: Mama J's Kitchen
ownershipEvidence: Venture Richmond's 2026 guide is explicitly titled '100+ Black-Owned Businesses to Check Out in Downtown Richmond' and lists Mama J's Kitchen at 415 N. 1st Street; WRIC identifies Lester Johnson as the owner of Mama J's Kitchen.
notes: Official site independently states the restaurant is family-owned and operated and gives 415 N. 1st Street, Richmond, VA 23219. Research-only; no publication or ingestion performed.
